evidence_separation.linguistic: Requires orthographic conventions (apostrophes/halants) to handle Munda checked consonants/glottal stops.
evidence_separation.dataset: Highly fragmented globally (Latin, Odia, Devanagari, Warang Citi). Devanagari is standard in Jharkhand schools.
evidence_separation.model_tokenizer: Devanagari is highly optimized in IndicTrans2 and NLLB. Warang Citi would cause severe token fragmentation.
evidence_separation.engineering: Simplifies UI rendering, avoids custom BPE training, aligns with Hindi hub.

key_findings.target_user_appropriateness: Hindi-medium teachers in Jharkhand can read it natively.
key_findings.linguistic_preservation: Possible, provided strict grapheme-to-phoneme rules are enforced for checked consonants.
key_findings.unicode_normalization: Requires standard NFC and strict conventions for glottal stops.
key_findings.tokenizer_compatibility: Excellent. Indic tokenizers support Devanagari natively.
key_findings.tts_asr_readiness: Fully feasible with custom G2P mapping.

final_verdict.rationale: It is the only script that satisfies both the pedagogical needs of the end-users (Hindi-medium teachers) and the computational realities of modern Indic NLP tokenizers.
